result:
I found 11 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings, and fixed all of them. After the fix, every one of the 150 rules gives the same result as a reference version I built from the docstrings, on boundary and large `qty` × `unit` inputs (0 mismatches).

| Rule | What it did wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 19, 40 | Discount started at 11 units instead of 10 | `qty >= 10` |
| 21, 52, 144 | Capped the price before taking the percentage (`min(base, cap) * pct`) | Take the percentage first, then cap the discount |
| 51, 53 | Rounded with `round()` | Round down with `//`, per the module docstring |
| 74 | Whole rule but used the marginal formula `(qty-12)*…` | `base * 12 // 100` |
| 118 | Cap only applied when the discount was over 60,000 | Cap at 30,000 always |
| 136, 145 | Marginal rules but discounted all units | `(qty - threshold) * unit * pct // 100` |

**Rules I left alone:** 16 other rules (13, 27, 31, 42, 43, 44, 46, 54, 59, 67, 117, 123, 125, 129, 135, 138) are written differently, e.g. `20 <= qty`, `not qty < 5`, or `if disc > cap`. They all give the same results as their docstrings, so I didn't change them. Rule 67 starts at `qty >= 31` instead of 30, but it's a marginal rule, so the discount at exactly 30 units is 0 anyway and the result is the same.

There are no tests in the repo, so the check was with my own script, outside the repo in `/tmp/chk/`.

STATUS: DONE
